title: Turn a UI screenshot into reusable components
summary: You provide a screenshot or mockup of a screen, and an AI tool builds it as reusable components in your project instead of one-off styles, extending the project's component catalog first and then composing the screen from it.

interview.question: What image will the automation work from?
options: A screenshot or mockup I will provide each time
Exported images from our Figma file
A mix of both, depending on the run
interview.mapsTo: Task instruction: the visual source the automation implements from.

interview.question: Where should the finished components live?
options: In our Storybook, so the team can browse them
In the project's component folder, following its existing structure
interview.mapsTo: Task instruction and required output files: the destination convention.

interview.question: How closely must the result match the image?
options: Match the design system first, small differences are fine
Match the image as closely as possible
interview.mapsTo: Task instruction: the fidelity priority between design-system consistency and pixel accuracy.

contractHints.instructionTemplate: Implement the provided <visual-source> as reusable components. Inventory the UI building blocks first, extend <destination-convention> with any missing components, then compose the screen from documented components. Prioritize <fidelity-priority>. Load the companion skill before deciding how to implement.
verificationHints: If package scripts contain build-storybook, use that script as the completion check.
If package scripts contain a build script for the app, use it to prove the new components compile.
Never write a completion check that repository evidence does not prove.
requiredArtifactHints: If the destination is Storybook, require the story files the project's conventions imply for the new components.
If no specific output path can be derived from repository evidence, leave the required files empty and state in the plain-language report that completion is judged by the completion checks alone.

prerequisites.description: The project has a component catalog or Storybook to extend.
prerequisites.evidence: A components directory matching the project's framework conventions, or a .storybook directory / storybook package script.
